'''''Disney Adventure''''' (originally named '''''Global Dream''''') is a [[cruise ship]] owned and operated by [[Disney Cruise Line]], a subsidiary of [[the Walt Disney Company]]. She is the eighth ship in the [[List of Disney Cruise Line ships|Disney Cruise Line fleet]] and the first and only current vessel of the {{sclass|Global|cruise ship|4}}, with her originally planned sister ship canceled. At {{GT|208,108|disp=long}}, ''Disney Adventure'' is one of the [[List of largest cruise ships|largest cruise ships in the world]] and the largest cruise ship ever built in Germany.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Portnews |date=September 2, 2025 |title=Wismar sends off Disney Adventure, the largest cruise ship built in Germany |url=https://en.portnews.ru/news/381271/ |access-date=January 27, 2026 |website=en.portnews.ru}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=September 10, 2025 |title="Disney Adventure" to be outfitted in Bremerhaven |url=https://hansa.news/disney-adventure-to-be-outfitted-in-bremerhaven/ |access-date=January 27, 2026 |website=hansa.news |language=en-US}}</ref> She is also the first [[Four-funnel liner|four-funnelled ocean-going passenger vessel]] since the retirement of the {{RMS|Aquitania||6}} in 1950.

She is planned to operate year-round from [[Marina Bay Cruise Centre Singapore]] until at least early 2031, marking Disney Cruise Line's first ship to be based outside the United States.<ref>{{Cite news |date=September 11, 2025 |title=First voyage of Disney's largest cruise ship from Singapore hits a snag |url=https://www.scmp.com/news/asia/southeast-asia/article/3325160/first-voyage-disneys-largest-cruise-ship-singapor |access-date=January 10, 2026 |work=South China Morning Post}}</ref> The itineraries feature a new concept for the company in which the ship itself is "both the journey and the destination," offering 3- and 4-night voyages entirely at sea with no port calls.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |date=September 11, 2025 |title=Check Out the All-New Disney Adventure Cruise Ship — Now Setting Sail March 2026! |url=https://www.undercovertourist.com/blog/disney-adventure/ |access-date=January 10, 2026 |website=Undercover Tourist}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Do Disney Adventure itineraries include ports of call? |url=https://disneycruise.disney.go.com/en-ph/faq/disney-adventure/itineraries/ |access-date=January 10, 2026 |website=disneycruise.disney.go.com |language=en}}</ref> However, on August 26th, 2026 (SGT time), Disney Cruise Line announced its first ever port call at Langkawi, Malaysia, on select sailings beginning from December 31st, 2026.<ref>https://www.disneyfoodblog.com/2026/08/25/the-disney-adventure-is-finally-getting-a-port-of-call/</ref><ref>https://www.traveltrendstoday.in/disney-adventure-adds-langkawi-as-new-port-of-call-from-dec-31</ref>

The vessel was originally ordered on May 11, 2016, by [[Genting Hong Kong]] for its [[Dream Cruises]] brand. Construction began with the [[keel laying]] on September 11, 2018, at the Rostock shipyard of [[MV Werften]], a Genting subsidiary. Progress was slowed by the COVID-19 pandemic, which contributed to the financial collapse of MV Werften and Genting. Disney purchased the vessel in 2022, estimated to be 60–80 percent complete, for €40{{Spaces}}million—far below its original €1{{Spaces}}billion valuation. After the acquisition, completion was overseen by [[Meyer Werft]] at MV Werften's former shipyard in Wismar, leased from [[TKMS]]. The interior was fitted with a reduced passenger capacity compared with the original plan. The [[Ceremonial ship launching|ship was launched]] on April 19, 2025, began [[sea trial]]s in September 2025, and was completed on December 12, 2025. Her maiden voyage took place on March 10, 2026. 

''Disney Adventure'' has a passenger capacity of approximately 6,700 and a gross tonnage of 208,108, making her 45% larger than the previous largest [[Disney Wish|''Wish''-class]] ships. She measures {{convert|342.7|meters}} in length, {{convert|46.4|meters}} in width, and is four decks taller than the ''Wish''-class vessels, with 1,954 staterooms. The ship is split into different neighbourhoods: Imagination Garden, Town Square, San Fransokyo Street, Marvel Landing, Discovery Reef, Wayfinder Bay and Toy Story Place. The ship is designed to use lower-emission [[methanol fuel]], though {{as of|2026|lc=y}} [[green methanol]] is not yet widely available in Singapore, and is equipped with [[Azimuth thruster|azimuthing podded propulsion]] (Azipod).

== History ==
=== Construction of the ''Global'' class ===
[[File:Global Dream under construction at MV Werften Warnemünde I.jpg|thumb|left|''Disney Adventure'' (then known as ''Global Dream'') under construction at the MV Werften Rostock shipyard in September 2019.]]
[[Genting Hong Kong]] ordered two ''Global'' class ships in May 2016 from its subsidiary [[Lloyd Werft]] for service with [[Star Cruises]], with delivery of the first vessel planned for 2019.<ref name="Genting">{{cite web |date=May 11, 2016 |title=Star Cruises orders two new mega cruise ships for China |url=http://www.cruiseandferry.net/articles/star-cruises-orders-two-new-mega-cruise-ships-for-china |access-date=September 9, 2023 |work=Cruise & Ferry}}</ref> In July 2016, Genting reorganized Lloyd Werft, creating [[MV Werften]] as a builder of large cruise ships.<ref>{{cite web |date=July 8, 2016 |title=Genting Hong Kong forms MV Werften to focus on newbuilds |url=http://www.cruiseandferry.net/articles/genting-hong-kong-forms-mv-werften-to-focus-on-newbuilds |access-date=March 14, 2018 |work=Cruise & Ferry}}</ref> In March 2018, Genting announced that the ships would instead be transferred to [[Dream Cruises]], operating from Chinese ports in summer and sailing to Southeast Asia, Oceania, and the west coast of the United States during the remainder of the year.<ref>{{cite web |date=March 12, 2018 |title=Genting to transfer Global Class newbuilds to Dream Cruises brand |url=http://www.cruiseandferry.net/articles/genting-to-transfer-global-class-newbuilds-to-dream-cruises-brand |access-date=March 14, 2018 |work=Cruise & Ferry}}</ref>

Because the design was not yet complete at the time of ordering, construction did not begin until March 8, 2018, when ceremonial steel cuttings were held at MV Werften's shipyards in [[Wismar]] and [[Rostock]]. Work on the first ship, ''Global Dream'', formally began that day.<ref>{{Cite web |title=News & Presse – MV WERFTEN |url=https://www.mv-werften.com/de/news-und-presse/news/mv-werften-startet-bau-des-ersten-204000-brz-grossen-global-class-kreuzfahrtschiffes-58.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606061513/https://www.mv-werften.com/de/news-und-presse/news/mv-werften-startet-bau-des-ersten-204000-brz-grossen-global-class-kreuzfahrtschiffes-58.html |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=September 13, 2023}}</ref> The [[keel]] was [[Keel laying|laid]] on September 11, 2018, in Rostock.<ref name="Keel">{{Cite web |title=News & Presse – MV WERFTEN |url=https://www.mv-werften.com/de/news-und-presse/news/erstes-schiff-der-global-klasse-fuer-dream-cruises-auf-kiel-gelegt.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606071020/https://www.mv-werften.com/de/news-und-presse/news/erstes-schiff-der-global-klasse-fuer-dream-cruises-auf-kiel-gelegt.html |archive-date=June 6, 2023 |access-date=September 13, 2023}}</ref> Major components were built at both yards, with final assembly taking place in Wismar. A large hull section was floated out of the Rostock dry dock on November 22, 2019, and towed to Wismar,<ref>{{cite web |title=DAS MITTSCHIFF DER "GLOBAL DREAM" WIRD NACH WISMAR TRANSPORTIERT |url=https://www.mv-werften.com/de/news-und-presse/news/das-mittschiff-der-global-dream-wird-nach-wismar-transportiert.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191213072237/https://www.mv-werften.com/de/news-und-presse/news/das-mittschiff-der-global-dream-wird-nach-wismar-transportiert.html |archive-date=December 13, 2019 |access-date=December 3, 2019 |language=german}}</ref> where it entered the dry dock the following day.<ref>{{cite web |date=November 3, 2019 |title=WISMARS SCHWIMMENDER GIGANT: DAS MITTSCHIFF DER "GLOBAL DREAM" IST ANGEKOMMEN |url=https://www.mv-werften.com/de/news-und-presse/news/wismars-schwimmender-gigant-das-mittschiff-der-global-dream-ist-angekommen.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191213072237/https://www.mv-werften.com/de/news-und-presse/news/wismars-schwimmender-gigant-das-mittschiff-der-global-dream-ist-angekommen.html |archive-date=December 13, 2019 |access-date=December 13, 2019 |language=german}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Global Dream Midsection Tow Underway – Cruise Industry News &#124; Cruise News |url=https://cruiseindustrynews.com/cruise-news/2019/11/global-dream-midsection-tow-underway/ |website=cruiseindustrynews.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Nachrichten aus Mecklenburg-Vorpommern |url=https://www.ndr.de/nachrichten/mecklenburg-vorpommern/Global-Dream-Mittschiff-in-Wismars-Hafen-eingelaufen,mvwerften228.html}}</ref>

Construction was scheduled to take just under three years, with the first ship to be delivered in late 2020 and the second in late 2021.<ref name="Genting2020">{{cite web |date=March 9, 2018 |title=MV Werften Starts Construction of 1st Global Class Ship |url=https://worldmaritimenews.com/archives/246800/mv-werften-starts-construction-of-1st-global-class-ship/ |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180309104313/https://worldmaritimenews.com/archives/246800/mv-werften-starts-construction-of-1st-global-class-ship/ |archive-date=March 9, 2018 |access-date=March 14, 2018 |work=World Maritime News}}</ref>

=== Purchase by Disney and naming ===
Due to the temporary closure of the shipyard in 2020 [[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany|as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic]], delivery of both ''Global''-class ships was expected to be delayed.<ref name="covid">{{cite web |date=July 6, 2020 |title=Troubled German yard group gets cash |url=https://www.motorship.com/news101/ships-and-shipyards/troubled-german-yard-group-gets-cash |access-date=July 11, 2020 |publisher=The Motorship}}</ref>

The pandemic's impact on tourism contributed to the collapse of Genting Hong Kong. MV Werften, Genting's German shipbuilding subsidiary, sought financial support from the German government to keep the shipyards operating but was unsuccessful. Hours after talks broke down, the company filed for bankruptcy on January 19, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tan |first=Weizhen |date=January 13, 2022 |title=Shares of cruise operator Genting Hong Kong plunge more than 50% as it warns of defaults |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2022/01/13/cruise-operator-genting-hong-kong-shares-plunge-after-default-warning.html |access-date=January 15, 2022 |website=CNBC |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=January 10, 2022 |title=Genting-owned Lloyd Werft also files for insolvency |url=https://www.seatrade-cruise.com/finance/genting-owned-lloyd-werft-also-files-insolvency |access-date=January 15, 2022 |website=seatrade-cruise.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":12">{{Cite web |date=January 19, 2022 |title=Cruise operator Genting Hong Kong files to wind up company |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/business/companies-markets/cruise-operator-genting-hong-kong-files-to-wind-up-company |access-date=January 22, 2022 |website=[[The Straits Times]] |language=en}}</ref>

On November 16, 2022, the insolvency administrator sold the first, partially completed ship, ''Global Dream'', to Disney Cruise Line for €40 million.<ref name="GlobalDream">{{cite web |last1=Meier |first1=Luiz |date=November 29, 2022 |title="Global Dream": 40 Mio. Euro für das größte Kreuzfahrtschiff der Welt |trans-title="Global Dream": 40 million euros for the largest cruise ship in the world |url=https://www.capital.de/wirtschaft-politik/-global-dream---40-mio--euro-fuer-das-groesste-kreuzfahrtschiff-der-welt-32959744.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221130164526/https://www.capital.de/wirtschaft-politik/-global-dream---40-mio--euro-fuer-das-groesste-kreuzfahrtschiff-der-welt-32959744.html |archive-date=November 30, 2022 |access-date=November 30, 2022 |website=capital.de |language=German}}</ref> The second, less complete vessel was sold for scrap. The Wismar shipyard itself was acquired by [[TKMS]] (ThyssenKrupp Marine Systems), with provisions allowing Disney Cruise Line's longtime shipbuilding partner, [[Meyer Werft]], to lease the facilities in order to complete the vessel.

At the time of the acquisition, Disney estimated that completing the ship would cost approximately US$1 billion, less than half the cost typically associated with constructing a new cruise ship. During the redesign process, Disney Imagineers substantially reworked the vessel to better align it with the company's family-oriented cruise model.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Fritz |first=Ben |date=January 9, 2026 |title=The 3,000-Person Team Working in Secret to Create Disney Magic |url=https://www.wsj.com/business/media/disney-cruise-rides-characters-imagineers-adventure-b5c03c1d |access-date=February 4, 2026 |website=The Wall Street Journal |language=en-US}}</ref> Passenger accommodations were reduced to 2,111 cabins, with a maximum capacity of approximately 6,000 passengers, in order to improve the passenger-to-crew service ratio.<ref name="ShipCrew">{{cite web |last=Sanders |first=Scott |date=October 16, 2024 |title=Disney Adventure Grand Reveal |url=https://disneycruiselineblog.com/2024/10/disney-adventure-grand-reveal/ |access-date=October 30, 2024}}</ref> The conversion proved more complex than initially anticipated, as the original design had been optimized for gambling-oriented cruise operations. Beginning in 2023, extensive structural modifications were undertaken, including the removal and relocation of internal steel supports, significant expansion of galley facilities, enlargement of entertainment venues, and the addition of multiple themed dining experiences.<ref name=":0" />

Disney's final cost for the vessel is estimated at US$1.8 billion, which remains about 10 percent less than the cost of constructing a newly built Disney cruise ship. According to the company, converting the existing hull also reduced the overall project timeline by several years compared with building a vessel from the keel up.<ref name=":0" />

Disney worked in collaboration with Meyer Werft to complete the vessel ahead of entry into service in 2026.<ref name="Service2025">{{Cite tweet |number=1597770549593518080 |user=scottgustin |title=One other note about Disney Cruise Line: At the D23 Expo, Disney announced the Disney Treasure will arrive in 2024. Today's filing says the Treasure will arrive in Fiscal 2025. Assuming these two claims are still accurate, the Treasure should arrive Oct–Dec. 2024. |first=Scott |last=Gustin |date=November 29, 2022 |access-date=November 30, 2022 |language=en |website=Twitter}}</ref> The vessel will be the largest ship in the Disney Cruise Line fleet and the first to be homeported year-round outside the United States, operating from [[Singapore Cruise |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240521052103/https://dclnews.com/2022/11/16/disney-cruise-line-announces-acquisition-of-ship-with-plans-to-visit-new-markets/ |archive-date=May 21, 2024 Today |language=en-US}}</ref>

The ship was delivered to Disney Cruise Line on December 13, 2025.<ref name="DNV">{{Cite ship register|id=37089|register=DNV|shipname=Disney Adventure|access-date=December 16, 2025}}</ref> It left Bremerhaven on January 4, 2026,<ref>{{Cite web |title=„Disney Adventure": Kreuzfahrtschiff verlässt Bremerhaven |url=https://www.nordsee-zeitung.de/bremerhaven/disney-adventure-bremerhaven-wartet-geduldig-auf-abfahrt-343231.html |access-date=January 11, 2026 |website=NZ-Online |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Abfahrt vorverlegt: „Disney Adventure" legt Sonntagmittag ab |url=https://www.nordsee-zeitung.de/bremerhaven/disney-adventure-legt-ab-hier-kann-die-abfahrt-beobachtet-werden-343026.html |access-date=January 11, 2026 |website=NZ-Online |language=de}}</ref> with stops made in [[Port Canaveral]], Florida,<ref>https://www.fox35orlando.com/news/disney-adventure-cruise-ship-arrives-port-canaveral-its-way-singapore.amp</ref> Los Angeles, California, and Tokyo, Japan. On February 2, 2026, the [[Panama Canal Authority]] announced that the ship is the largest by gross tonnage and passenger capacity [[Neopanamax]] cruise ship to cross the [[Panama Canal]], breaking the previous record held by ''[[Norwegian Bliss]]''.<ref>{{cite press release |title=The Panama Canal Marks Milestone with Transit of the Disney Adventure Cruise Ship |date=February 2, 2026 |url=https://pancanal.com/en/the-panama-canal-marks-milestone-with-transit-of-the-disney-adventure-cruise-ship/ |last1=Cleghorn |first1=Luis |website=Autoridad del Canal de Panamá}}</ref>

''Disney Adventure'' arrived at the [[Marina Bay Cruise Centre Singapore|Marina Bay Cruise Centre]] in Singapore on March 3, 2026, to a [[water salute]] and fireworks.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Chua |first=Leena |date=March 4, 2026 |title=Disney's newest cruise ship arrives in Singapore |url=https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/03/04/news/disneys-newest-cruise-ship-arrives-in-singapore/2292540 |access-date=March 3, 2026 |work=[[The Manila Times]] |language=en}}</ref> It was officially christened by godparent [[Robert Downey Jr.]] in a ceremony the following night, on March 4.<ref>{{Cite news |date=March 4, 2026 |title=Actor Robert Downey Jr christens Disney Adventure cruise ship at Marina Bay Cruise Centre |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/life/travel/actor-robert-downey-jr-christens-disney-adventure-cruise-ship-at-marina-bay-cruise-centre |access-date=March 4, 2026 |work=The Straits Times |language=en |issn=0585-3923}}</ref> On March 10, 2026, ''Disney Adventure'' entered service and embarked on her maiden voyage, sailing on a three-night cruise from Singapore and back.<ref>{{Cite web |title='Very, very excited': Passengers set off on Disney Adventure cruise's first voyage from S'pore |url=https://entertainment.inquirer.net/657996/very-very-excited-passengers-set-off-on-disney-adventure-cruises-first-voyage-from-spore |access-date=2026-03-19 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mitchell |first=Hattie |title=Disney Adventure cruise ship sets sail on maiden voyage {{!}} blooloop |url=https://blooloop.com/disney-adventure-cruise-maiden-voyage/ |access-date=2026-03-19 |website=blooloop.com |language=en}}</ref>

Beginning on December 31, 2026, select four-night cruises aboard the ''Disney Adventure'' will include a port stop at [[Langkawi]], [[Malaysia]]. The sailings with the port call will start with two days at sea, with the Langkawi  stop scheduled for the third day, and the fourth day being final day and night at sea.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-08-25 |title=Disney Adventure four-night sailings with Langkawi stop |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/life/travel/disney-adventure-launches-four-night-sailings-with-stop-in-langkawi-from-dec-31 |access-date=2026-08-25 |work=The Straits Times |language=en |issn=0585-3923}}</ref>

==Design==
[[File:Disney Adventure Disney Cruise Line (55114525115).jpg|thumb|left|Stern view of the Disney Adventure, showing her four funnels.]]
The ship was originally planned at {{GT|201,000|disp=long}}, and the final design measured over {{GT|208,000|link=off}}.<ref name="Genting" /> She measures {{convert|342|m|ftin|sp=us}} in length, with a [[Beam (nautical)|beam]] of {{convert|46.4|m|ftin|sp=us}} and a [[Draft (hull)|draft]] of {{convert|9.5|m|ftin|sp=us}}.<ref name="Genting2020" />

Propulsion is provided by six [[MAN Diesel & Turbo|MAN]] 48/60CR engines with a combined output of {{convert|96,000|kW|hp|lk=on}}. The engines generate power for three [[Azipod]] XO thrusters through ACS6080 variable frequency drives, all built by [[ABB]].<ref>{{cite web |date=November 17, 2016 |title=MV Werften Selects MAN Engines for New Cruise Ships |url=https://www.marinelink.com/news/werften-selects-engines418463 |access-date=March 14, 2018 |website=Marine Link}}</ref><ref name="pst">{{cite web |date=January 10, 2017 |title=ABB scoops contract for five new Genting cruise ships |url=http://www.passengership.info/news/view,abb-scoops-contract-for-five-new-genting-cruise-ships_45999.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180315133532/http://www.passengership.info/news/view,abb-scoops-contract-for-five-new-genting-cruise-ships_45999.htm |archive-date=March 15, 2018 |access-date=March 14, 2018 |work=Passenger Ship Technology}}</ref> ABB also supplied control components and software.<ref name="pst" />

''Disney Adventure'' was designed to operate on [[methanol fuel]]. However, [[green methanol]] was not available in Singapore at the time the ship entered service. The vessel instead operates on a mix of sustainable and lower-emission fuels, including [[hydrotreated vegetable oil]] (HVO).<ref name="Maritime Executive">{{Cite web |date=January 15, 2026 |title=Disney's Ultra-Large Cruise Ship Makes U.S. Stop on Delivery Run to Asia |url=https://maritime-executive.com/article/disney-s-ultra-large-cruise-ship-makes-u-s-stop-on-delivery-run-to-asia |access-date=February 6, 2026 |website=The Maritime Executive |language=en}}</ref>

The vessel has [[Four-funnel liner|four funnels]], the first Disney ship to have more than two.<ref name="Adventure Updates">{{Cite web |date=December 16, 2025 |title=Disney Adventure Updates: News from the High Seas |url=https://disneyparksblog.com/dcl/disney-cruise-line-adventure-updates/ |access-date=January 9, 2026 |website=Disney Parks Blog |language=en-US}}</ref> It is the first ocean-going passenger vessel built with four funnels since {{Ship|RMS|Aquitania||6}}, which operated from 1914 to 1950.<ref name="auto" /> As with earlier Disney ships, not all funnels are functional, and the vessel's two forward funnels are dummy funnels. As such, it is also the first four-funnel passenger vessel with dummy funnels since {{Ship|RMS|Windsor Castle|1921|6}} and {{Ship|RMS|Arundel Castle||6}}, which carried four funnels until 1937.<ref name="auto" />

The original ''Global''-class design was to incorporate [[artificial intelligence]] systems and robotic technologies for passenger services, including voice and facial recognition.<ref>{{cite web |date=March 9, 2018 |title=Construction starts on first Global-class cruise ship |url=https://www.bairdmaritime.com/work-boat-world/passenger-vessel-world/1789-construction-starts-on-first-global-class-cruise-ship |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180315133538/https://www.bairdmaritime.com/work-boat-world/passenger-vessel-world/1789-construction-starts-on-first-global-class-cruise-ship |archive-date=March 15, 2018 |access-date=March 14, 2018 |publisher=Baird Maritime}}</ref> That design provided for 2,350 passenger cabins with capacity for 9,000 passengers, including 4,700 in lower berths, and a crew of 2,200.<ref>{{cite web |date=October 16, 2019 |title=Global Dream Hull art revealed |url=https://cruiseshipprofiles.com/2019/10/17/global-dream-hull-art-revealed |access-date=November 17, 2022 |work=Cruise Ship Profiles}}</ref> Under Disney, the design was revised to include 2,111 passenger cabins with capacity for 6,000 passengers.<ref name="ShipCrew" />

==Recreation==
===On-board activities===
The ship features seven themed areas, conceptually similar to lands at Disney theme parks: Disney Discovery Reef, Toy Story Place, Wayfinder Bay, Marvel Landing, San Fransokyo Street, Town Square, and Disney Imagination Garden.<ref name="Adventure Updates" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Disney Adventure Themed Areas |url=https://disneycruise.disney.go.com/ships/adventure/themed-areas/? |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241207105351/https://disneycruise.disney.go.com/ships/adventure/themed-areas/? |archive-date=December 7, 2024 |access-date=February 15, 2026 |website=Disney Cruise Line |language=en}}</ref>

Disney Imagination Garden includes the Storybook Castle, described by the company as its first physical Disney castle created as an art installation aboard a ship. The structure rises three decks and is styled to resemble a pop-up storybook.<ref name="Adventure Updates" />

Marvel Landing includes the ''Ironcycle Test Run'', designed by [[Maurer AG]] and described as Disney's first roller coaster at sea. At the time of the ship's launch, it was reported to be the longest roller coaster at sea, extending more than {{convert|820|ft|m}}.<ref name="Adventure Updates" /> The area also includes two additional rides with lower height requirements: ''Pym Quantum Racers'' and ''Groot Galaxy Spin''.
 
''Disney Adventure'' is the first ship since the ''Disney Wonder'' that does not have an [[AquaDuck]] (or AquaMouse on the ''Wish''-class) water slide. Instead, Woody and Jessie's Wild Slides, a pair of water slides located at Toy Story Place, stand in place of the AquaDuck.

On the second night of the ''Disney Adventure'' cruise, guests will be able to watch a fireworks show: "The Lion King: Celebration in the Sky", narrated by [[Shah Rukh Khan]]. This makes Disney Cruise Line the only cruise line in the world to offer fireworks at sea; the other ships in the Disney Cruise Line fleet also feature fireworks shows. Disney has this exclusive entertainment feature because they use biodegradable compressed air fireworks, which are completely harmless to the marine environment.

===Entertainment===
''Disney Adventure'' contains the following entertainment venues:
* Garden Theatre (live original productions: ''Avengers Assemble!'', Let's Set Sail, ''Duffy and The Friend Ship'' and ''Baymax Super Exercise Expo'')
* Wayfinder Bay (live original production: ''Moana: Call of the Sea'')
* Walt Disney Theatre (live original productions: ''Remember'' and ''Disney Seas the Adventure'')
* Baymax Cinemas (screens motion pictures)

===Dining===
Every night of a ''Disney Adventure'' cruise, guests dine at a different restaurant. This is called "rotational dining". On a Disney ship, guests rotate along with their servers, which helps develop the relationship between diner and wait staff.

There are six rotational dining restaurants on the ''Disney Adventure'':
* Hollywood Spotlight Club (deck 8 aft)
* Navigator's Club (deck 6 aft)
* Animator's Palate (deck 5 aft, also featured on four of the other Disney cruise ships)
* Animator's Table (deck 9 aft)
* Enchanted Summer Restaurant (deck 6 midship)
* Pixar Market Restaurant (deck 17 aft)

Because each voyage only lasts three to four nights, it is not possible to visit all six restaurants in one sailing. Thus, the rotational dining on the ''Disney Adventure'' is divided into three districts, with two restaurants per district, and guests are randomly assigned to one restaurant in each district. In addition, unlike other Disney Cruise Line ships, the ''Disney Adventure'' does not have its own buffet location. Therefore, the Enchanted Summer and Pixar Market restaurants function as buffets during breakfast and lunch. Two premium dining restaurants are available at an additional cost: Mike and Sulley's Flavors of Asia (deck 10 aft) and Palo Trattoria (decks 10 and 11 aft), the latter which is exclusively for adults.
